Horrid staff, second-rate food
Mar 2023 • Friends
I’ve been coming to La Plancha at least once a month or every other month for the past many years. 

The food was never incredible, but it’s been consistent and the prices—along with the menu—have never changed. That is, until recently. 

Food quality and presentation have really tumbled down hill. The potatoes dauphinoise that accompanied my duck magret were soggy and inedible—tasted like they were made a week prior and frozen for a quick reheat. And the pate special tasted like it was from a can and poorly presented with a wilted looking salad. 

Beyond the food, however, the most unpleasant part is dealing with the sullen, near braindead wait staff. And based on other reviews, I'm not alone here. 

Here's an example:

One of the reasons that I liked going to La Plancha was that the restaurant serves cheap (but decent) wine in a jug with the options of rose, cabernet or two different whites. 

But the past two times I went, the rose was out (or I later learned, they just stopped selling it). Okay, fine, I tried ordering both of the whites—they were “out” too. The only option left was red. Mind you, La Plancha has a rather large wine room so I found it hard to believe that there was no wine comparably priced that they could substitute. 

Since our server could barely utter a word of English, I politely asked if a manager was around who I could speak to. Annoying, the server sent over ANOTHER server—not the manager—to speak to me. Odd, considering I saw the manager (who I assume also owner) walking around the indoor dining room.

I didn’t get very far with this server either despite explaining the situation and telling her how it could easily be remedied. 

Beyond that interaction, I've yet to come to La Plancha and be greeted in a cheerful, welcoming way. All the servers are cold and seem like they haven't a clue what they're doing. Not to mention, if you have any questions about the menu, it's always a blank stare (this is the same when I've come with Vietnamese friends). 

I realize that the economy isn’t doing well at the moment, but cutting corners at the expense of consistent customers is a BAD idea when the chips are down. I suspect the owner of La Plancha owns the building and likely doesn’t care if it turns a profit or not. Almost every time I’ve been there, the place is practically empty. 

These days there are so many restaurants in D2, and while La Plancha fit that “sweet spot” years ago, I’m afraid it no longer does. 

There need to be some changes because otherwise, I can’t picture it being open much longer.
